subject: Re: Performance SLOs & regional routing — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs, regional routing, next steps

Thanks for taking the time today, Sarah — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical sync: 

Key performance/behavior items you shared:
- Latency targets: 95th pct <= 250ms for short-text generation (<=128 tokens) in US/EU; target 95th pct <= 350ms for APAC (initial).
- Throughput: steady-state ~12k requests/minute, peaks up to 30k/min during batch windows.
- Concurrency: expected 400 concurrent sessions across regions (US 200, EU 120, APAC 80).
- Streaming: many endpoints will use streaming (token-by-token) for assistant flows; must support chunked responses and resume semantics for reconnections.
- Data residency: EU PII must stay in EU region; APAC testing data can live in APAC but main production data resides in US/EU depending on customer region.

Deliverables we mentioned:
1) I attached an initial SLO matrix (finova-slo-matrix.xlsx) with itemized latency/availability targets and suggested fallback policies.
2) Aditya will propose a regional routing + model variant plan to meet these targets (canary + capacity tiers).
3) We’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and security teams next week to validate KMS/keys and data residency controls.

Next steps: 
- Aditya and David: can you prepare the regional routing sketch + estimated GPU footprint and warm-up times by Thu 26 Feb?
- Sarah: confirm availability for the technical sync (ask: Tue/Wed next week).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: finova-slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@finova.com>, Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs, regional routing, next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the 250ms (95th) in US/EU is for synchronous single-shot generation (<=128 tokens). For multi-turn chat (streaming), we care about <100ms first-byte for token streaming after the first token, and overall tail for longer responses should not exceed the 95th target by more than 100ms.
- Throughput: the 30k/min peak is a 45-minute burst we see during our nightly summary jobs (EU-heavy).
- Concurrency: concurrent sessions will be sticky to region based on user location; we may ask for geo-pin for EU users to keep PII inside EU.
- Data residency: important — any PII tagged records for EU customers must be stored and processed within the EU region (including logs used for eval). We will require evidence of region-isolation for both model inference and logging.

For the technical sync: Tue 3/2 or Wed 3/3 afternoon PT works for our infra and security. Please send a calendar invite.

Rajesh, looping in procurement for timing on legal/NDA and anticipated contract timeline.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Lee
Director of Product, Finova
sarah.lee@finova.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs, regional routing, next steps

Thanks Sarah — digging into the numbers now. High-level thoughts and an initial plan: 

1) Regional routing approach\- a) Geo-aware routing by IP/latency with hard pinning option for EU accounts. b) Use model variants: a lower-latency quantized variant for US/EU short generation; a slightly higher-throughput variant for APAC to reduce GPU pressure.

2) Capacity & concurrency estimate (preliminary)\- Based on 12k steady / 30k peak: ~8 p100-equivalent GPUs for steady plus autoscale headroom to 20 GPUs during peaks depending on model size and batching. Concurrency 400 distributed across regional pools (US: 200, EU: 120, APAC: 80).

3) Streaming\- Redwood supports chunked streaming and reconnect tokens. We'll expose a streaming SLO: first-byte <=100ms (95th) for streaming after warm-up and delivery of token batches every 50-100ms depending on model throughput.

4) Data residency / logging\- We can configure per-account routing + region-limited logging. For EU PII we will route inference and store logs in EU-only buckets; we can provide audit proofs (SOC2 summary attached) and a write-up of log-retention controls for the technical sync.

I attached a quick architecture sketch (redwood-arch-diagram.pdf) and the SOC2 summary. I'll put a more detailed capacity table in the Drive folder and share the link.

Action: I'll have a detailed capacity + warm-up plan and recommended model variants by Fri 27 Feb so we can review in the tech sync on Tue 3/3.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (diagram, 240KB); soc2-summary.pdf (8KB)

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finova.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:41:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs, regional routing, next steps

Appreciate the detail — Finova is keen to proceed with a 6-week PoC scoped to US+EU first. A couple of asks from procurement/security: 

1) Can you provide the SOC2 summary and a short-itemized evidence list for EU data isolation (what logs, where they are stored, who can access)?
2) Proposed PoC dates: start 3/16, runway 6 weeks, with a mid-PoC check on week 3. We need an estimated cost range for that period to circulate to budget owners (rough order of magnitude is fine).
3) We will prepare a short mutual action plan and DocuSign for the PoC engagement — looping procurement for legal.

If you can share the PoC cost estimate and the evidence checklist before the tech sync on Tue 3/3 it will help accelerate.

Thanks,
Rajesh

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

- Aditya is finalizing the capacity table + estimated GPU hours for the 6-week PoC; we’ll provide a rough cost range by EOD Mon 3/8.
